title: MedMamba: Multi-View State Space Models with Adaptive Graph Learning for Medical Time Series Classification
claim: Medical time series pose intertwined challenges: slow drift masks local patterns, and channel dependencies shift between segments, motivating multi-view and adaptive modeling.
layout: 3 panels: top-left, top-right, bottom row; color-coded boxes and matrices
description: The figure has three panels illustrating challenges in medical time series classification. Panel (a), top left, shows a noisy blue signal over a smooth gray baseline-drift curve. An orange box highlights a local event, and arrows label both the drift and the event. Panel (b), top right, shows the raw signal with arrows pointing down to two derived views: a green temporal-difference trace and a purple frequency spectrum with a yellow highlighted peak. Panel (c), bottom, shows five stacked multichannel traces, C1 to C5, in different colors. A blue box and a red box mark two segments. An arrow labeled 'adaptive dependencies' leads to two blue 5x5 heatmap matrices, A1 with a blue border and A2 with a red border. The matrices differ between the two segments. Bold serif captions sit under each panel. The eye lands first on the large noisy waveform in (a).
caption: Key challenges in MedTS classification. (a) Baseline drift can obscure discriminative local morphology. (b) Complementary raw, temporal difference, and frequency-domain views provide robust cues under drift. (c) Cross-channel dependencies vary across segments. Dependency matrices (\textcolor[rgb]{0.35,0.46,0.70}{$A_1$}, \textcolor[rgb]{0.82,0.28,0.35}{$A_2$}) are from two highlighted segments extracted from the same recording.
abstract: Medical time series are central to healthcare, enabling continuous monitoring and supporting timely clinical decisions. Despite recent progress, existing methods struggle to jointly model local-global dynamics and handle nonstationarities like baseline drift, while often failing to capture latent channel interactions. To address these challenges, we propose MedMamba, an end-to-end architecture that integrates state space models with domain-specific inductive biases. Specifically, MedMamba first employs multi-scale convolutional embeddings to capture discriminative local morphology. Second, to mitigate nonstationarity, we introduce a tri-branch differential state space encoder that processes raw, temporal-difference, and frequency-domain views, fusing them to emphasize informative patterns while suppressing drift. Furthermore, to uncover latent channel correlations, we design a spatial graph Mamba module that learns a directed dependency structure regularized toward sparsity and acyclicity, which obviates the need for predefined graphs. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that MedMamba achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining linear computational complexity, and ablation studies validate each component's contribution.Code is available at https://github.com/zhangda1018/MedMamba.
